The transaction is an unauthorized charge or billing error by a merchant the customer previously interacted with in their local region.

events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: The customer has disputed transaction 3530164 ($49.00). A review of the card's 72-hour history reveals extreme volatility in billing addresses (addr1 ranging from 143.0 to 476.0) and associated email domains (gmail.com, anonymous.com, bellsouth.net, and me.com), indicating a high likelihood of card compromise or account takeover.
key_points: The disputed transaction 3530164 occurred on 2016-12-10 with an address code of 330.0 and email domain 'me.com'.
Transactions 3521954 and 3522026 on 2016-12-07 also utilized the same 330.0 address code but had no associated email address.
The card shows highly suspicious velocity and geographic/address dispersion within 72 hours, including a high-value transaction of $1749.88 (3525595) at address 143.0.

events.assessment: Customer C08623 has reported an unauthorized $49.00 transaction (3530164), which aligns with a severe historical pattern of fraud on their account. Between August and October 2016, the customer was victimized in five separate confirmed fraud cases, primarily involving out-of-region card-present transactions and one account takeover. Given this extensive history of compromise, the current claim is highly credible and indicates ongoing targeting of this customer.
key_points: Customer C08623 has five prior confirmed fraud cases (CC-2817, CC-2935, CC-3327, CC-3682, and CC-4957) totaling over $1,150 in fraudulent exposure.
Four of the historical cases were classified as 'out_of_region_use' involving card-present transactions, while case CC-3327 was an 'account_takeover' involving mixed-channel activity.
Despite previous actions to block and reissue the card (C08623-K2) in multiple cases, the customer continues to experience unauthorized activity.

knowledge: Card-not-present fraud from a new device

issues: The draft violates R7: The disputed transaction is in billing region 330.0, where the card has 42 prior purchases, matching the customer's own recurring pattern. R7 dictates CREATE_CASE + VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER + WARN_CUSTOMER and explicitly states 'do not block'. The draft incorrectly applied R2 and blocked the card.
The draft violates R1: The fraud probability is 0.66 (under 0.70), which requires VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER or STEP_UP_AUTH before any block.

The specialist notes hallucinate evidence not present in the case data, including 'extreme volatility in billing addresses' and multiple email domains (transaction specialist), as well as 'five separate confirmed fraud cases' (precedent specialist), which directly contradicts the evidence showing only one prior false alarm.
events.what_would_change_verdict: If the customer confirms the transaction upon verification (R3), the case would be closed as no fraud. If the customer insists it is fraud despite the recurring pattern, and further investigation rules out family fraud or confusion, the verdict would remain fraud and the card would be blocked.
